name: Barskoon Gorge
near: Barskoon is a village on the southern highway at the entrance to the gorge (approx. 140 km from Balykchy, 80–90 km from Karakol); it is 17–20 km up the valley to the site with the Gagarin monuments and the waterfalls (faheyjamestravel 2024: 17 km; firsov.kz: 20 km).
elev: The gorge entrance ~2000 m (Destination Jeti Oguz); above 2800 m — spruce forests and juniper (2GIS); Sary-Moynok Pass 3442 m, Barskoon Pass 3816 m, the Arabel plateau ~3770 m (firsov.kz 2019; Destination Jeti Oguz). The elevation of the waterfall site was not found (approximately 2300–2500 m — not confirmed).
short: A gorge on the southern shore of Issyk-Kul with a cascade of waterfalls (“Snow Leopard's Tears” 24 m, “Manas's Bowl”, “Champagne Spray”, “Elder's Beard”), two Gagarin monuments and an excellent gravel Kumtor road leading over 3800 m passes to the syrts (high plateaus) of Arabel.
desc: The valley of the Barskoon River cuts into the Terskey Ala-Too for 30–40 km from the village of the same name. Below are steppe grasses and shrubs, above 2800 m — Tian Shan spruce and juniper, and above them the peaks of the Panfilov Heroes (4610 m) and the World Peace Council (4310 m). 17–20 km from the village is the main site: a bust and a “face in stone” of Yuri Gagarin (the cosmonaut vacationed here after his 1961 flight), a monument to a KamAZ truck — to the builders of the road to Kumtor, seasonal cafe yurts and parking. From here trails lead to the waterfalls: “Snow Leopard's Tears” (24 m, ~1.5 h climb, a legend about a snow leopardess mourning her cubs), “Manas's Bowl”, “Champagne Spray” and “Elder's Beard”. The road through the gorge is one of the best dirt roads in the country: it is maintained year-round by the Kumtor gold mine, so it is passable for a passenger car even in winter and leads over the Sary-Moynok (3442 m) and Barskoon (3816 m) passes to the Arabel plateau with its lakes; higher up is the Kumtor checkpoint (the drive to the plateau is open, the mine territory is closed). Entry to the gorge is free (2024).
guide: The main thing here is not to drive to the waterfalls but to walk to them: from the parking by Gagarin to “Snow Leopard's Tears” is an hour and a half of steep trail with a gain of about 350 m, but the water falls as a 24-metre wall. First pay your respects to Gagarin — the two monuments and the KamAZ on a pedestal look surreal among the spruces, and it is real history: the cosmonaut vacationed on Issyk-Kul in 1961. If you have half a day and a clear sky — drive on along the Kumtor gravel road: an hour of switchbacks and you are at 3800 m, on the syrts of Arabel, with lakes and yaks. Don't drink the river water — the mine is upstream; the springs on the slopes are clean. A taxi from the village — a guide figure of 1600 som, and horses at the yurts are offered “depending on the mood”, so haggle.
see: The waterfalls “Snow Leopard's Tears” (24 m), “Manas's Bowl”, “Champagne Spray”, “Elder's Beard”; the monuments to Gagarin (a bust and a bas-relief in the rock) and the KamAZ; spruce and juniper forests; the switchbacks up to Sary-Moynak Pass and Barskoon Pass (3816 m) with views of the lake; the Arabel plateau with its lakes (separate entry); the Petrov Glacier by Kumtor (not for visiting).
skip: You are not ready for a steep hour-and-a-half climb — the waterfalls can't be seen from the parking. You are already heading to Arabel with an overnight — you will see the gorge on the way. In rain: the trail to the waterfalls is slippery and dangerous.
diff: Driving through the gorge — easy (a passenger car). The trail to “Snow Leopard's Tears”: 3.1 km, +367 m, ~2.5 h round trip, “strenuous” (faheyjamestravel, 2024); to the third waterfall another +45 min (kyrgyzstan-tourism.com). The climb to the passes — altitude 3400–3800 m.
when: May–October for the waterfalls (maximum water flow — June–July, snowmelt); September — quiet and golden. The road is maintained year-round (Destination Jeti Oguz); in winter — the waterfalls are frozen, the passes depend on the weather.
hours: Open terrain, open 24 hours, no ticket offices (faheyjamestravel 2024: “open all day and night”). The Kumtor checkpoint is higher up the road — a vehicle inspection, the drive to the plateau is open (firsov.kz 2019, pikabu 2021).
daytime: Morning — set out from Barskoon by 8–9 a.m. to climb to the waterfalls before the heat and thunderstorms; in the second half of the day the light on the waterfalls is better for photos, but the trail is busier.
how: Along the southern highway Balykchy — Karakol to the village of Barskoon (marshrutka (minibus) from Karakol 100–150 som, from Bishkek 250–500 som — visitkarakol.com; fresher prices above), then south on the Kumtor gravel road for 17–20 km to the site with the Gagarin monuments (a taxi from the village ~1600 som, 2024). On foot from the village — 4–5 h. Beyond that — trails to the waterfalls or the road to the passes and Arabel.
needcar: Yes, from the village to the waterfalls it is 17–20 km with no public transport; a passenger car is fine (2GIS, firsov.kz). Hitchhiking is realistic because of the Kumtor traffic.
self: Yes: the road is obvious, no permits needed (the Kumtor checkpoint lets tourists through to the plateau after inspection), the trails to the waterfalls are well trodden; an offline map is advisable.
roadtype: Paved road along the highway to the village; then the Kumtor gravel road — “an excellent dirt road, packed down by trucks”, passable for a sedan and a motorcycle (firsov.kz 2019, pikabu 2021, too.kg); to the waterfalls — walking trails, steep, slippery after rain.
traveltime: Karakol — Barskoon ~1.5–2 h; village — waterfall site 30–40 min; the trail to “Snow Leopard's Tears” ~1.5 h up, 2.5 h round trip; a whole day from Barskoon with a walk — ~6 h (kyrgyzstan-tourism.com). Transfer Karakol — waterfalls — Karakol: 200 km, ~4 h of pure driving (MYWAY).
stay: In the village of Barskoon: guesthouses (Ryskeldi Guest House and others), CBT; in Tamga — a sanatorium and guesthouses; at the waterfall site — seasonal cafe yurts and camping (too.kg, firsov.kz). 2025–2026 prices not found.
net: Too.kg: coverage is “partial”; in the village of Barskoon all operators have a signal; at the waterfalls the signal is unstable, on the passes and plateau — absent (too.kg/arabel). The operator and the test date are not specified.
entry: Free (faheyjamestravel, 2024; kyrgyzstan-tourism.com 2023 — no fee mentioned). Only parking/yurts/horses, where available, are paid. Check on site.
transfer: Taxi Barskoon — waterfalls 1600 som (2024); Karakol — Barskoon 4500–5000 som (2024); MYWAY Karakol — waterfalls — Karakol 9,900 som per minivan (2026); marshrutka (minibus) Karakol — Barskoon 100–150 som (date not given).
bring: Trekking shoes and poles (the trail is steep), a rain jacket, water (don't drink from the river — the mine is upstream; the springs are clean), a warm jacket for the passes (3800 m), cash for the yurts and taxis, an offline map, a reserve of fuel for the trip to the plateau.
warn: Water in the Barskoon River is not recommended for drinking because of the Kumtor mine upstream (too.kg). The trail to the waterfalls is steep and slippery after rain. Kumtor trucks on the road — keep to the side. The mine territory is closed, the checkpoint is above the passes; the 3400–3800 m passes — altitude sickness with a rapid ascent. Haggle at the yurts and with the horse owners.
food: Cafe yurts at the waterfalls (seasonal): shashlik, lagman, kumis, tea; in the villages of Barskoon and Tamga — ashkana (small eateries) and home cooking at guesthouses. Specific places and prices were not checked.
reviews: 2GIS “Barskoon Gorge”: 5.0/5, 55 ratings, 24 reviews (07.10.2026). Google — separate markers “Barskoon Waterfall” and “Gagarin Monument” (ratings not captured). Pros per 2019–2024 reports: road quality, the 24 m waterfall, the monuments, free; cons — the steep trail, pushy horse owners, dust from trucks.
p.sum: From the village of Barskoon on the southern highway it is 17–20 km along the excellent Kumtor mine gravel road to the site with the Gagarin monuments and cafe yurts — any passenger car can do it. Without your own car: a marshrutka (minibus) from Karakol to Barskoon (~100–150 som) + a taxi from the village (~1,600 som per car, 2024) or a taxi from Karakol (3,500–5,000 som one way). From the parking, a steep trail leads to the “Snow Leopard's Tears” waterfall (3.1 km, +367 m, ~2.5 h round trip). Overnight in Tamga or Barskoon; after 17:00 it is hard to find transport out of the gorge.

p.iti.2.title: A southern-shore combination
p.iti.2.plan: Karakol → Jeti-Oguz → Barskoon (waterfalls) → Arabel → Tamga → Skazka → Bokonbaevo.
p.season: May–June — maximum water, mud on the trail; July–August — yurts and horses are working, afternoon thunderstorms; September — quiet, golden; October–April — the road is open (Kumtor clears it), the waterfalls are frozen, no yurts.
p.budget.economy: Marshrutka (minibus) Bishkek — Barskoon 500–600 / Karakol — Barskoon ~100–150; a taxi from the village ~1,600 per car (÷3); free entry; a guesthouse in Tamga ~1,200–1,900/person ≈ 2,000–3,000 som/person.
p.budget.comfort: MYWAY from Karakol 9,900 per car (÷4 ≈ 2,500); Tamga Guesthouse 3,800 for a double; lunch in a yurt. ≈ 5,000–7,000 som/person.
p.permits: No permits needed. Above the waterfalls is a document-check checkpoint (passport, vehicle documents); the Kumtor mine territory is closed.
p.access: The site by Gagarin is accessible to everyone (from the parking), the trail to the waterfalls is not for strollers and older people (steep); children from 7–8 years old. Dogs are allowed.
